facts.statement: Fossils of Yuanmousaurus include nine dorsal vertebrae, three sacral vertebrae, and seven caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: From the trunk and tail, nine dorsal, three sacral and seven caudal vertebrae were found.

facts.statement: The ratio of humerus length to thigh bone length in Yuanmousaurus was 0.72.
facts.quote: the length ratio between humerus and thigh bone was 0.72 in Yuanmousaurus, while it was 0.56 in Shunosaurus and 0.80 in Omeisaurus.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Yuanmousaurus, YMV 601, was collected in May 2000 in the village of Jiangyi, Yuanmou County, Yunnan Province.
facts.quote: The only known specimen, YMV 601, was collected in May 2000 in the village Jiangyi in Yuanmou County, Yunnan Province.

facts.statement: Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis was named by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2006.
facts.quote: They were described as belonging to a new genus and species, named Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis, by Lü Junchang and colleagues in 2006.

facts.statement: Yuanmousaurus lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 165 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Yuanmousaurus lived between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago, from the Aalenian to the Callovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Callovian (174.7 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Many paleontologists have abandoned the family Euhelopodidae because the systematic position of Euhelopus is controversial.
facts.quote: Euhelopodidae, sin embargo, es abandonado por muchos paleontólogos ya que la posición sistemática de Euhelopus en sí es controvertida.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Yuanmousaurus is a valid genus, as it may be considered dubious.
facts.quote: It may be a dubious genus.
